explanation_en: The pronominal verb 'verse' combined with an adjective or participle ('verse obligado/a/os/as') is a common way to express how someone finds themselves in a certain state or situation. It sounds more natural and objective than simply using 'estar obligado a' or 'tener que'.

examples.en_text: Due to the crisis, the company has found itself forced to reduce its staff.
examples.target_text: Debido a la crisis, la empresa se ha visto obligada a reducir su personal.

examples.en_text: The director has found himself forced to cancel this afternoon's meeting due to a last-minute problem.
examples.target_text: El director se ha visto obligado a cancelar la reunión de esta tarde por un problema de última hora.

examples.en_text: Many neighbors have found themselves forced to change their cars because of the new pollution regulations.
examples.target_text: Muchos vecinos se han visto obligados a cambiar sus coches por las nuevas normas de contaminación.

examples.en_text: The schools in the area have found themselves forced to suspend classes due to the severe storm.
examples.target_text: Las escuelas de la zona se han visto obligadas a suspender las clases por el fuerte temporal.

examples.en_text: She has found herself forced to look for a second job to be able to pay the apartment rent.
examples.target_text: Ella se ha visto obligada a buscar un segundo trabajo para poder pagar el alquiler del piso.

examples.en_text: The tourists have found themselves forced to stay at the hotel due to the transport strike.
examples.target_text: Los turistas se han visto obligados a quedarse en el hotel por la huelga de transporte.

explanation_en: In Spanish legal and political contexts, 'devolución en caliente' refers to the immediate pushback or summary deportation of migrants at the border without formal legal procedures. The idiom 'en caliente' generally means 'on the spot' or 'in the heat of the moment', but in this specific collocation, it has a precise geopolitical meaning.

examples.en_text: The migrants who jumped the Ceuta fence were summarily deported without being able to apply for asylum.
examples.target_text: Los migrantes que saltaron la valla de Ceuta fueron devueltos en caliente sin poder pedir asilo.

examples.en_text: The European Court of Human Rights has debated whether it is legal for a foreigner to be immediately pushed back.
examples.target_text: El Tribunal Europeo de Derechos Humanos ha debatido si es legal que un extranjero sea devuelto en caliente.

examples.en_text: Several organizations denounce that many people are summarily deported at the southern border.
examples.target_text: Varias organizaciones denuncian que muchas personas son devueltas en caliente en la frontera sur.

examples.en_text: The police detained the young men at the border and summarily deported them that same night.
examples.target_text: La policía detuvo a los jóvenes en la frontera y los devolvió en caliente esa misma noche.

examples.en_text: According to current law, those who enter illegally can be pushed back immediately.
examples.target_text: Según la ley actual, los que entran de forma ilegal pueden ser devueltos en caliente inmediatamente.

examples.en_text: She tried to cross the river, but was discovered by the guards and immediately pushed back to her country.
examples.target_text: Ella intentó cruzar el río, pero fue descubierta por los guardias y devuelta en caliente a su país.

explanation_en: Originally a military term meaning to tighten the formation of soldiers, 'cerrar filas' is widely used in politics and business to mean showing a united front or rallying behind a leader, especially during a crisis or under external criticism.

examples.en_text: In the face of the current crisis, the party members decided to close ranks around their leader.
examples.target_text: Ante la crisis actual, los miembros del partido decidieron cerrar filas en torno a su líder.

examples.en_text: When things get difficult, our family always closes ranks to help each other.
examples.target_text: Cuando las cosas se ponen difíciles, nuestra familia siempre cierra filas para ayudarse.

examples.en_text: The coach asked us to close ranks and stay united for the next game.
examples.target_text: El entrenador nos pidió que cerremos filas y nos mantengamos unidos para el próximo partido.

examples.en_text: The employees closed ranks to defend the project against criticism from the press.
examples.target_text: Los empleados cerraron filas para defender el proyecto contra las críticas de la prensa.

examples.en_text: It is time for us neighbors to close ranks and demand more safety in the neighborhood.
examples.target_text: Es hora de que los vecinos cerremos filas y exijamos más seguridad en el barrio.

examples.en_text: The board of directors is closing ranks to prevent the company from splitting.
examples.target_text: La junta directiva está cerrando filas para evitar que la empresa se divida.

idiom: más viejo que el hilo negro
explanation_en: A highly idiomatic Spanish expression used to describe something that is extremely old, outdated, or a well-known cliché. It is equivalent to the English 'older than the hills' or 'older than dirt'. It adds a very native, colloquial flavor to speech.

examples.en_text: That joke you told me is older than the hills; my grandfather already knew it.
examples.target_text: Ese chiste que me contaste es más viejo que el hilo negro; ya se lo sabía mi abuelo.

examples.en_text: I don't know why you still keep that mobile phone, it's older than the hills and doesn't have internet.
examples.target_text: No sé por qué todavía guardas ese teléfono móvil, si es más viejo que el hilo negro y no tiene internet.

examples.en_text: That excuse about forgetting your keys is older than the hills; make up something better.
examples.target_text: Esa excusa de que se te olvidaron las llaves es más vieja que el hilo negro; inventa algo mejor.

examples.en_text: Although you think you've discovered a new fashion trend, wearing wide pants is older than the hills.
examples.target_text: Aunque pienses que has descubierto una nueva moda, llevar pantalones anchos es más viejo que el hilo negro.

examples.en_text: That love story between those two is older than the hills, the whole neighborhood knows about it.
examples.target_text: Esa historia de amor entre ellos dos es más vieja que el hilo negro, todo el barrio la conoce.

examples.en_text: The trick of studying at the last minute is older than the hills and almost never works.
examples.target_text: El truco de estudiar a última hora es más viejo que el hilo negro y casi nunca funciona.

explanation_en: An adverbial phrase meaning 'on a daily basis' or 'every day'. It is often preferred over 'diariamente' in spoken Spanish for its natural flow and ease of pronunciation. It can modify verbs or stand as a time adverbial.

examples.en_text: I usually take the subway daily to go to the office.
examples.target_text: Suelo tomar el metro a diario para ir a la oficina.

examples.en_text: It is important to drink enough water daily to stay hydrated.
examples.target_text: Es importante beber suficiente agua a diario para mantenerse hidratado.

examples.en_text: She checks her email daily so she doesn't miss any important messages.
examples.target_text: Ella revisa su correo electrónico a diario para no perderse ningún mensaje importante.

examples.en_text: My grandfather goes out for a walk daily in the neighborhood park.
examples.target_text: Mi abuelo sale a caminar a diario por el parque del barrio.

examples.en_text: If you practice Spanish daily, you will notice a big improvement in a few months.
examples.target_text: Si practicas español a diario, notarás una gran mejora en pocos meses.

examples.en_text: In this house we cook daily because we prefer fresh food.
examples.target_text: En esta casa cocinamos a diario porque preferimos la comida fresca.

explanation_en: Means 'together', 'jointly', or 'as a whole'. It is a very common collocation used in professional and collaborative contexts to describe teamwork or coordinated efforts between different entities.

examples.en_text: If we work together, we will finish the project much faster.
examples.target_text: Si trabajamos en conjunto, terminaremos el proyecto mucho más rápido.

examples.en_text: We made the decision together after discussing all the options.
examples.target_text: Tomamos la decisión en conjunto después de discutir todas las opciones.

examples.en_text: You must evaluate the situation as a whole and not just look at the small problems.
examples.target_text: Debes evaluar la situación en conjunto y no solo ver los pequeños problemas.

examples.en_text: The colors of the room look very good together.
examples.target_text: Los colores de la sala se ven muy bien en conjunto.

examples.en_text: The two departments analyzed the data together for the report.
examples.target_text: Los dos departamentos analizaron los datos en conjunto para el informe.

examples.en_text: The team achieved victory thanks to the collective effort of all the players.
examples.target_text: El equipo logró la victoria gracias al esfuerzo en conjunto de todos los jugadores.

explanation_en: The verb 'consistir' always requires the preposition 'en' in Spanish. This phrase is the standard way to ask or explain the nature, components, or details of a task, concept, or project.

examples.en_text: Could you explain to me what exactly your new job consists of?
examples.target_text: ¿Podrías explicarme en qué consiste exactamente tu nuevo trabajo?

examples.en_text: I don't quite understand what the project you presented yesterday consists of.
examples.target_text: No entiendo bien en qué consiste el proyecto que presentaste ayer.

examples.en_text: The doctor explained to me what the tests they are going to do to me consist of.
examples.target_text: El médico me explicó en qué consisten las pruebas que me van a hacer.

examples.en_text: Before we start playing, tell us what this board game consists of.
examples.target_text: Antes de empezar a jugar, dinos en qué consiste este juego de mesa.

examples.en_text: In yesterday's interview they asked me what my previous job consisted of.
examples.target_text: En la entrevista de ayer me preguntaron en qué consistía mi anterior empleo.

examples.en_text: I want to sign up for the course, but first I need to know what it consists of.
examples.target_text: Quiero apuntarme al curso, pero primero necesito saber en qué consiste.

explanation_en: A set phrase meaning 'generally', 'usually', or 'as a rule'. It is widely used in both speech and writing to describe common occurrences, habits, or patterns, serving as a synonym for 'generalmente'.

examples.en_text: Generally, the weather in this region is quite mild during the autumn.
examples.target_text: Por lo general, el clima en esta región es bastante templado durante el otoño.

examples.en_text: Generally, I prefer to work from home on Fridays to avoid the traffic.
examples.target_text: Por lo general, prefiero trabajar desde casa los viernes para evitar el tráfico.

examples.en_text: Supermarkets, generally, close earlier on Sundays and holidays.
examples.target_text: Los supermercados, por lo general, cierran más temprano los domingos y días festivos.

examples.en_text: Generally, the people in this town are very friendly to tourists.
examples.target_text: Por lo general, la gente de este pueblo es muy amable con los turistas.

examples.en_text: I don't usually drink coffee in the afternoon because, generally, it keeps me awake.
examples.target_text: No suelo tomar café por la tarde porque, por lo general, me quita el sueño.

examples.en_text: Final exams, generally, represent forty percent of the grade.
examples.target_text: Los exámenes finales, por lo general, representan el cuarenta por ciento de la nota.
